blocks.text: The rate constant k of a reaction can be calculated by two methods: the initial concentration (initial rates) method, and the half-life method for first-order reactions.

blocks.caption: The two methods
rows: Initial rates at several known concentrations
k = rate / (product of concentrations to their orders)
Time for the concentration to halve

blocks.prompt: Which method could be used for a second-order reaction, and why?
blocks.explanation: The initial concentration method, because it works for any order: measure the initial rate at known concentrations and divide by the concentration terms of the rate law. The simple half-life relation k = 0.693 / t1/2 holds only for first-order reactions, whose half-life is independent of concentration.

items: Two routes to k: initial rates at known concentrations (any order), and the half-life relation k = 0.693 / t1/2 (first order).
